name: Auxetic suture
subtitle: a stitch that gets fatter when pulled

effects.effect: a material gets fatter when stretched

effect: a material gets fatter when stretched
how: Repaired shoulder tendons fail in a quarter or more of patients, often because the thin stitches slice through the soft tendon like a cheese wire when the arm is used. This suture is braided so that it gets fatter instead of thinner when pulled, spreading the load over more tendon exactly when the pull is hardest.
obstacle: Swelling by a fraction of a millimetre may not be enough, and the braid must stay smooth enough to slide through tissue and hold a knot.
why: Turns the stitch's worst moment into its widest; whether the gain is big enough is untested.
real: Searched auxetic/negative-Poisson's-ratio braided sutures; found only conventional cut-through studies and auxetic tendon tissue/scaffold work, no auxetic suture.
